_: AI Debt Tracker, WEEK 6. Every number here is transcribed from the author's own saved results as published in pantry/*.svg and in narration_script.md's source table and notes. Each bar's geometry in those SVGs was recomputed as a ratio and had to agree with its printed fraction before the value was accepted. Nothing in this file is estimated, rounded for the frame, or typed from memory.

merge._geom: shared linear scale, 6.0 px per bond. Week 5 bar 156.0/6.0 = 26. Week 6 bar 18.0/6.0 = 3. Same unit, same baseline x=250.
merge.what: bonds the tracker added that the target report does not hold
merge.same: same readings, same 45 quarters, B0's opening ledger
merge.undiagnosed: The three that are left are not yet diagnosed.
merge._actions_note: These are counts of what the merge step DID across the run. They are NOT a breakdown of the 26 — week 5's 26 broke down as 10 + 10 + 4 + 2. Conflating the two would be a real error, so the frame labels them as actions.

actions.what: launch notices folded into the priced bond that followed
bonds named with no amount held as questions, not added
the banks' option to buy more recorded, not added

merge.is_code: The merge step is code, not a model.
merge.loans: Loans are handled now too: a drawn amount counts as debt, a new commitment does not, and a repayment reduces it.

opening._: the opening-ledger reader — the crutch this week removes

steps.what: scores the report's tables and keeps the ones that look like a debt note
points at the rows that are one bond or loan, and at their kind — it types no number
reads every value from the cited cell and the row's own label; the header decides which column is the period end when it can

opening.rule_from: the same rule the event reader has followed since week 1
opening.was: Until now every quarter started from a ledger taken from the answer key.
opening.was_light: That is cheating a little, and it was deliberate.

score.reports_read_what: opening reports of the development quarters
score.graded_note: The figure's own source line says GRADED AT L1, 43 REPORTS. The 94 is how many were read; 43 is the denominator the two percentages are measured on, and the frame says so.
score.verdict: The model adds recall, not precision.

defects.what: Two code defects on the first pass: a rate column read as the amount, and a unit lost from a caption the parser cut short.
defects.fixed_on: development data; every report was re-read and both passes are reported

variance._: the same report, asked twice, answered differently — no bar, because the point is that there is no single number
variance.why: The first pass stored only the first 3,000 characters of each model answer, so nine long answers could not be reused and were asked again.
variance.what_it_means: The model's pointing is not the same from run to run. That variance is part of what the reader is, and it is reported rather than averaged away.
variance.unknown: One run per report cannot say how often a swing like this happens.

gap.graded_what: development quarters graded bond by bond

starts.label: B0 carry forward
starts.note: still borrows the answer key's start

gap.why_precision_rose: Fewer bonds held means fewer held wrongly.
gap.vs_b0: Against B0: recall -0.9 points (-9.4 to +6.0) — level. Precision +2.6 points.
gap.the_point: The +7.0 points of recall over doing nothing was the borrowed ledger. Reading its own start, the agent is level with B0 on recall and ahead on precision.

where._: the gap is concentrated, not spread — which is why it can be worked on

cases.what: the opening reader found 23 instruments across two quarters whose reports hold 39 and 40
its opening reports were filed the same day as the report being predicted, so the point-in-time rule refuses them to the agent

where.refused_what: opening reports the point-in-time rule refuses — Core Scientific's amendments and two late Super Micro reports
where.rule_doing_its_job: That is the rule doing its job, and it is counted in the gap rather than worked around.

wrong.label: ended wrong, and the checks flagged it

right.label: ended right, and the checks flagged it anyway

catch.settled_what: Most of them were bonds the opening ledger already held, so dropping the question confirms the ledger rather than changing it.
catch._settled_conflict: FRICTIONAL.md breaks the 21 down as 19 + 2; description.txt as 17 + 2 + 2. Both sum to 21 and they disagree on the split, so NO breakdown is drawn — only the 21, and the part both sources agree on. FACTCHECK records the conflict.
catch.still_open: All 24 maturity questions stayed open, because the passages the model pointed at gave no due date. 15 repayments are still unexplained.
catch.investigators: Investigators now run inside the graph, one per open question, at most two rounds.

total_debt.what: quarters whose total debt lands within 2% of the report

limits.same_key: The opening-ledger reader was graded against the same answer key that supplies the oracle start.
limits.no_fresh_triage: There was no fresh triage set this week, so all three triage sets are now calibrations.

handcheck.what: Alphabet's euro notes are keyed at their dollar carrying amount — logged, not fixed against the set that found it

limits.test_split: Everything here is on development quarters; the test split has not been touched.

truthcheck._: who produced the judgments — not a person
truthcheck.model_judgments: Which table rows are instruments, and which passage states a missing value, are qwen3:4b's judgments, flagged in every record. Every number in a ledger was parsed by code.
truthcheck.handcheck_by: The hand-check transcriptions are a model's reading, not a person's.

next: then version 1: freeze, scale up, run the whole development window unattended
